items.stem: 'Yoga is a way of life'. What makes it a way of life?
items.answer: Yoga is not limited to physical postures, breathing techniques or meditation done for a few minutes; rather yoga is a way of life also. It propounds several principles and practices, such as asana, pranayama, kriya, mudra, bandha and meditation, which are relevant to healthy living. As a way of life it gives direction about food, eating habits, thinking, recreational means and conduct, and its components are ahara (food), vihara (relaxation), achara (conduct), vichara (thinking) and vyavahara (behaviour or actions). These yogic principles and practices of healthy living can be adopted by all, irrespective of age, gender, profession or place. A yogic way of life, if adopted in the true sense, empowers us to deal with stress and promote physical and mental health.
grounding: Rather yoga is a way of life also.
It propounds several principles and practices, such as, asana, pranayama, kriya, mudra, bandha and meditation which are relevant to healthy living.
Yogic principles and practices of healthy living can be adopted by all, irrespective of age, gender, profession or place.
As a way of life, yoga gives direction about food, eating habits, thinking, recreational means and conduct.
Vyavahara (behaviour) means actions. Vyavahara is the result of ahara, vihara, achara and vichara.
Yogic way of life, if adopted in true sense, empowers us to deal with stress and promote physical and mental health.

items.stem: Which specific Yoga practices are relevant for relaxation?
items.answer: The yogic practices of asana, pranayama and meditation relax body and mind. Among the asanas, Makarasana is a relaxing asana to body and mind and is very beneficial for reducing stress, and Shavasana (corpse posture) is a relaxing practice. Anuloma-viloma pranayama (alternate nostril breathing) relaxes the body and mind, and Bhramari pranayama is also a relaxing pranayama. Yoganidra relaxes body and mind and reduces tension, so it too is helpful in the management of stress.
grounding: Yogic practices of asana, pranayama and meditation relax body and mind.

Anuloma-viloma pranayama (Alternate Nostril Breathing) relaxes the body and mind.
therefore it is named as Bhramari Pranayama. It is a relaxing pranayama.

items.stem: List any two positive and two negative effects of stress on body.
items.answer: Positive effects: (i) stress which motivates us to perform better and learn new skills is beneficial; (ii) situations such as getting admission in a new course, preparing for an examination or getting a promotion cause stress, but this stress is beneficial as it finally contributes towards growth and development. Negative effects: (i) when stress is severe and chronic it reduces the efficiency of a person and may adversely affect our ability to feel, think and act; (ii) it can lead to various psychosomatic diseases such as peptic ulcer, migraine, diabetes mellitus and high blood pressure, and could even result in heart attack, brain stroke and death.
grounding: Stress which motivates us to perform better and learn new skills is beneficial.
getting admission in a new course, preparing for an examination or getting promotion may cause stress but this stress is beneficial as it finally contributes towards growth and development
When stress is severe and chronic it reduces efficiency of a person. This kind of stress may adversely affect our ability to feel, think and act.
It can lead to various psychosomatic diseases, such as, peptic ulcer, migraine, diabetes mellitus, high blood pressure, etc.
It could even result in heart attack, brain stroke and death.

items.stem: Write any two symptoms of stress under each of these heads: Physiological symptoms, Emotional symptoms, Behavioral symptoms.
items.answer: Physiological symptoms: changes in heart rate and pulse rate, and a change in blood pressure (the chapter also lists altered secretion of hormones). Emotional symptoms: anger and fear (the chapter's psychological-level list also includes hate and sadness). Behavioral symptoms: becoming restless and worried, and being unable to focus on studies, with even small things causing irritation or making the person angry.
grounding: At the physiological level, there may be changes in heart rate, pulse rate, blood pressure, secretions of hormones, etc.
At the psychological level, there may be changes in attention, concentration, memory and alertness and also in the emotional state (like anger, fear, hate, sadness, etc.).
During severe stress, people may become restless and worried. They may not remember the things properly. Even small things may make them angry.
You may not be able to focus on your studies and small things may cause irritation.

items.stem: You are stressed due to a certain happening. Mention any two yogic practices you would like to perform to de-stress yourself. Give reasons.
items.answer: Two suitable practices are Shavasana and anuloma-viloma pranayama. Shavasana is chosen because it is very effective for de-stressing the body and mind, which remain in a state of rest, and because it helps to reduce blood pressure, anxiety and insomnia and gives relief to the tired body and mind. Anuloma-viloma pranayama is chosen because it relaxes the body and mind and lowers stress by developing harmony in the various systems of the body, and because it helps in managing stress by reducing anxiety.
grounding: This asana is very effective for de-stressing the body and mind which remain in a state of rest.
It helps to reduce blood pressure, anxiety and insomnia and gives relief to the tired body and mind.
Anuloma-viloma pranayama (Alternate Nostril Breathing) relaxes the body and mind.
It lowers stress by developing harmony in various systems of the body.
It helps in managing stress by reducing anxiety.

items.stem: Write the advantages of the following yogic practices: 1. Shirshasana
items.answer: Shirshasana is the head stand posture, in which one stands on one's head. Its advantages are: it improves blood circulation, particularly of venous blood; it helps in the proper functioning of the abdominal organs and the endocrine glands; and it increases the supply of blood to the brain and strengthens the central nervous system.
grounding: In this posture one stands on one's head, hence it is called Shirshasana (Head Stand Posture).
It improves blood circulation, particularly of venous blood.
It helps in the proper functioning of the abdominal organs and endocrine glands.
It increases the supply of blood to the brain and strengthens the central nervous system.

items.stem: Write the advantages of the following yogic practices: 2. Anuloma- Viloma Pranayama
items.answer: Anuloma-viloma pranayama (alternate nostril breathing) relaxes the body and mind. It calms down the mind and improves concentration. It nourishes the body with oxygen, purifies the blood and improves the efficiency of the brain, and it improves the functioning of all the cells of the body by providing them sufficient oxygenated blood. It improves blood supply to the brain and helps to regulate blood pressure. It helps in managing stress by reducing anxiety, and it is beneficial in many diseases such as asthma, high or low blood pressure, insomnia, chronic pain, endocrine imbalances, heart problems and hyperactivity.
